title: Nonarchimedean prime-power sum and root error bounds
statement:
Let $E$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a nonarchimedean real absolute value. Write $E^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], and let $p>0$ be the characteristic of $E^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$. Let $n\ge0$, $q=p^n$, $t\ge1$, and $x_1,\ldots,x_t\in E$. Then
$$\left|\left(\sum_{i=1}^t x_i\right)^q-\sum_{i=1}^t x_i^q\right|\le |p|\max_{1\le i\le t}|x_i|^q.$$
For $u,v\in E$ one also has
$$|(u-v)^q-(u^q-v^q)|\le |p|\max(|u|,|v|)^q.$$
If $y_1,\ldots,y_t,y\in E$ satisfy $y_i^q=x_i$ and $y^q=\sum_{i=1}^t x_i$, then, for every such choice of roots,
$$\left|y-\sum_{i=1}^t y_i\right|\le |p|^{1/q}\max_{1\le i\le t}|x_i|^{1/q}.$$
Here $p$ in an absolute value denotes its image in $E$; all roots of nonnegative real numbers denote their nonnegative real roots.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.10(i)--(ii), printed p. 46; difference form by the same binomial estimate (including the sign term when p=2).

proof.text: Set $c=|p|$. The nonarchimedean axiom gives $|m\cdot1_E|\le1$ for every integer $m$: use induction for positive $m$ and $|-a|=|a|$ for negative $m$. Thus $0\le c\le1$, and if $p\mid m$ then $|m\cdot1_E|\le c$ by multiplicativity. The residue quotient is a field: an element of $E^\circ$ outside $\{a:|a|<1\}$ has norm $1$, hence its inverse also lies in $E^\circ$. Its positive characteristic $p$ is prime, since a factorization $p=ab$ with $1<a,b<p$ would give two nonzero elements with zero product in that field. Also $q=p^n\ge1$. If $n=0$, then $q=1$: both power errors are zero and the stipulated roots are $y_i=x_i$, $y=\sum_i x_i$, so all three assertions hold. Henceforth assume $n>0$.

proof.text:
For $0<j<q$, one has $v_p(j)<n$: otherwise $q=p^n$ divides the positive integer $j<q$. Apply [lem-pur-prime-power-binomial-divisibility] with $a=n$ and $k=j$. Since $n-v_p(j)\ge1$, it gives $p\mid\binom qj$, and Step 1 gives $|\binom qj|\le c$. Apply [lem-pur-commutative-ring-binomial-expansion] in $E$ to $a,b\in E$. After removing the two endpoint terms, each remaining monomial has norm at most $c M^q$, where $M=\max(|a|,|b|)$, because $|a|^j|b|^{q-j}\le M^q$. The finite-sum bound [lem-trf-nonarchimedean-finite-sums], applied with $N=|\cdot|$ to this nonempty finite sum, yields
$$|(a+b)^q-a^q-b^q|\le c\max(|a|,|b|)^q.$$
The bound also covers $M=0$, when $a=b=0$.

proof.text:
Put $M=\max_i|x_i|$ and $S_j=\sum_{i=1}^j x_i$. The finite-sum bound [lem-trf-nonarchimedean-finite-sums] with $N=|\cdot|$ gives $|S_j|\le M$. Induct on $1\le j\le t$ with claim $|S_j^q-\sum_{i=1}^j x_i^q|\le c M^q$. For $j=1$ the error is zero. For the induction step write the new error as
$$(S_j+x_{j+1})^q-S_j^q-x_{j+1}^q+\left(S_j^q-\sum_{i=1}^j x_i^q\right).$$
Step 2 bounds the first summand by $c M^q$, and the induction hypothesis bounds the second by the same number. The ultrametric inequality proves the claim at $j+1$. At $j=t$ it is the first asserted bound.

proof.text:
Apply Step 2 to $u,-v$. If $p$ is odd then $q$ is odd, so $(-v)^q=-v^q$ and this is the difference bound. If $p=2$, then $q$ is even, and
$$(u-v)^q-(u^q-v^q)=\big((u-v)^q-u^q-(-v)^q\big)+2v^q.$$
The first summand has norm at most $c\max(|u|,|v|)^q$ by Step 2, and the second has norm $|2||v|^q=c|v|^q$. The ultrametric inequality gives the same bound. These cases exhaust primes $p$; in characteristic $2$ the last summand is simply zero.

proof.text:
For the stipulated roots put $B=\sum_i y_i$ and $R=\max_i|y_i|$, so $R^q=\max_i|x_i|$. Multiplicativity and the finite-sum bound [lem-trf-nonarchimedean-finite-sums] with $N=|\cdot|$ give $|B|\le R$ and
$$|y|^q=|\sum_i x_i|\le\max_i|x_i|=R^q,$$
hence $|y|\le R$ because $q\ge1$. Step 3, applied to the $y_i$, gives $|B^q-y^q|\le c R^q$. Step 4, applied to $y,B$, gives $|(y-B)^q-(y^q-B^q)|\le c R^q$. Adding these two errors and applying the ultrametric inequality yields $|y-B|^q\le c R^q$. Taking nonnegative real $q$-th roots proves
$$|y-\sum_i y_i|\le c^{1/q}R=|p|^{1/q}\max_i|x_i|^{1/q}.$$
If $R=0$ the same inequalities force $y=B=0$; if $c=0$ they force $y=B$. Thus this argument also covers zero inputs and equal characteristic, and it applies to every choice of roots without asserting their existence.

lean.statement: theorem nonarchimedean_prime_power_root_estimates {E : Type u} [Field E] (abv : AbsoluteValue E ℝ) (hna : IsNonarchimedean abv) (A : ValuationSubring E) (hA : ∀ z : E, z ∈ A ↔ abv z ≤ 1) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) [CharP (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) p] (n t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (x : Fin t → E) : abv ((∑ i : Fin t, x i) ^ (p ^ n) - ∑ i : Fin t, x i ^ (p ^ n)) ≤ abv (p : E) * (⨆ i : Fin t, abv (x i)) ^ (p ^ n) ∧ (∀ a b : E, abv ((a - b) ^ (p ^ n) - (a ^ (p ^ n) - b ^ (p ^ n))) ≤ abv (p : E) * max (abv a) (abv b) ^ (p ^ n)) ∧ (∀ (ys : Fin t → E) (y : E), (∀ i : Fin t, ys i ^ (p ^ n) = x i) → y ^ (p ^ n) = ∑ i : Fin t, x i → abv (y - ∑ i : Fin t, ys i) ≤ abv (p : E) ^ (1 / ((p ^ n : ℕ) : ℝ)) * (⨆ i : Fin t, abv (x i)) ^ (1 / ((p ^ n : ℕ) : ℝ)))
